verses.original: Καὶ συνάγονται πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καί τινες τῶν γραμματέων ἐλθόντες ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων
verses.transliteration: Kai synagontai pros auton hoi Pharisaioi kai tines tōn grammateōn elthontes apo Hierosolymōn
verses.literal: Then the Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around . . . Jesus
verses.literalPt: E AJUNTARAM-SE a ele os fariseus, e alguns dos escribas que tinham vindo de Jerusalém.

verses.original: καὶ ἰδόντες τινὰς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ὅτι κοιναῖς χερσίν τοῦτ’ ἔστιν ἀνίπτοις ἐσθίουσιν τοὺς ἄρτους
verses.transliteration: kai idontes tinas tōn mathētōn autou hoti koinais chersin tout’ estin aniptois esthiousin tous artous
verses.literal: and they saw some of His disciples eating . . . . . . with hands that were defiled that is unwashed
verses.literalPt: E, vendo que alguns dos seus discípulos comiam pão com as mãos impuras, isto é, por lavar, os repreendiam.

verses.original: Οἱ γὰρ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ πάντες οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἐὰν μὴ πυγμῇ νίψωνται τὰς χεῖρας οὐκ ἐσθίουσιν κρατοῦντες τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων
verses.transliteration: Hoi gar Pharisaioi kai pantes hoi Ioudaioi ean mē pygmē nipsōntai tas cheiras ouk esthiousin kratountes tēn paradosin tōn presbyterōn
verses.literal: Now in holding to the tradition of the elders the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat until . . . they wash their hands ceremonially
verses.literalPt: Porque os fariseus, e todos os judeus, conservando a tradição dos antigos, não comem sem lavar as mãos muitas vezes;

verses.original: καὶ ἀπ’ ἀγορᾶς ἐὰν μὴ βαπτίσωνται οὐκ ἐσθίουσιν καὶ ἄλλα πολλά ἐστιν ἃ παρέλαβον κρατεῖν βαπτισμοὺς ποτηρίων καὶ ξεστῶν καὶ χαλκίων καὶ κλινῶν
verses.transliteration: kai ap’ agoras ean mē baptisōntai ouk esthiousin kai alla polla estin ha parelabon kratein baptismous potēriōn kai xestōn kai chalkiōn kai klinōn
verses.literal: And on returning from the market they do not eat unless . . . they wash And there are many other traditions for them to observe including the washing of cups pitchers kettles and couches for dining
verses.literalPt: E, quando voltam do mercado, se não se lavarem, não comem. E muitas outras coisas há que receberam para observar, como lavar os copos, e os jarros, e os vasos de metal e as camas.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐπερωτῶσιν αὐτὸν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς Διὰ τί οὐ περιπατοῦσιν οἱ μαθηταί σου κατὰ τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων ἀλλὰ κοιναῖς χερσὶν ἐσθίουσιν τὸν ἄρτον
verses.transliteration: Kai eperōtōsin auton hoi Pharisaioi kai hoi grammateis Dia ti ou peripatousin hoi mathētai sou kata tēn paradosin tōn presbyterōn alla koinais chersin esthiousin ton arton
verses.literal: So the Pharisees and scribes questioned Jesus Why . . . do Your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders Instead they eat . . . . . . with defiled hands
verses.literalPt: Depois perguntaram-lhe os fariseus e os escribas: Por que não andam os teus discípulos conforme a tradição dos antigos, mas comem o pão com as mãos por lavar?

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Καλῶς ἐπροφήτευσεν Ἠσαΐας περὶ ὑμῶν τῶν ὑποκριτῶν ὡς γέγραπται ὅτι Οὗτος ὁ λαὸς τοῖς χείλεσίν με τιμᾷ Ἡ δὲ καρδία αὐτῶν πόρρω ἀπέχει ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ
verses.transliteration: Ho de eipen autois Kalōs eprophēteusen Ēsaias peri hymōn tōn hypokritōn hōs gegraptai hoti Houtos ho laos tois cheilesin me tima Hē de kardia autōn porrō apechei ap’ emou
verses.literal: Jesus answered them Isaiah prophesied correctly about you hypocrites as it is written These people honor Me with their lips but their hearts are far from Me
verses.literalPt: E ele, respondendo, disse-lhes: Bem profetizou Isaías acerca de vós, hipócritas, como está escrito: Este povo honra-me com os lábios, Mas o seu coração está longe de mim;

verses.original: Μάτην δὲ σέβονταί με Διδάσκοντες διδασκαλίας ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων
verses.transliteration: Matēn de sebontai me Didaskontes didaskalias entalmata anthrōpōn
verses.literal: They worship Me in vain they teach as doctrine the precepts of men
verses.literalPt: Em vão, porém, me honram, Ensinando doutrinas que são mandamentos de homens.

verses.original: Ἀφέντες τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ κρατεῖτε τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν ἀνθρώπων
verses.transliteration: Aphentes tēn entolēn tou Theou krateite tēn paradosin tōn anthrōpōn
verses.literal: You have disregarded the commandment of God to keep the tradition of men
verses.literalPt: Porque, deixando o mandamento de Deus, retendes a tradição dos homens; como o lavar dos jarros e dos copos; e fazeis muitas outras coisas semelhantes a estas.

verses.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Καλῶς ἀθετεῖτε τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἵνα τὴν παράδοσιν ὑμῶν τηρήσητε
verses.transliteration: Kai elegen autois Kalōs atheteite tēn entolēn tou Theou hina tēn paradosin hymōn tērēsēte
verses.literal: He went on to say You neatly set aside the command of God to maintain your own tradition
verses.literalPt: E dizia-lhes: Bem invalidais o mandamento de Deus para guardardes a vossa tradição.

verses.original: Μωϋσῆς γὰρ εἶπεν Τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα σου καί Ὁ κακολογῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα θανάτῳ τελευτάτω
verses.transliteration: Mōusēs gar eipen Tima ton patera sou kai tēn mētera sou kai Ho kakologōn patera ē mētera thanatō teleutatō
verses.literal: For Moses said Honor your father and your mother and Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death
verses.literalPt: Porque Moisés disse: Honra a teu pai e a tua mãe; e quem maldisser, ou o pai ou a mãe, certamente morrerá.

verses.original: ὑμεῖς δὲ λέγετε Ἐὰν εἴπῃ ἄνθρωπος τῷ πατρὶ ἢ τῇ μητρί Κορβᾶν ὅ ἐστιν Δῶρον Ὃ ἐὰν ἐξ ἐμοῦ ὠφεληθῇς
verses.transliteration: hymeis de legete Ean eipē anthrōpos tō patri ē tē mētri Korban ho estin Dōron Ho ean ex emou ōphelēthēs
verses.literal: But you say that if a man says to his father or mother Whatever . . . you would have received from me is Corban (that is a gift devoted to God )
verses.literalPt: Vós, porém, dizeis: Se um homem disser ao pai ou à mãe: Aquilo que poderias aproveitar de mim é Corbã, isto é, oferta ao Senhor;

verses.original: οὐκέτι ἀφίετε αὐτὸν οὐδὲν ποιῆσαι τῷ πατρὶ ἢ τῇ μητρί
verses.transliteration: ouketi aphiete auton ouden poiēsai tō patri ē tē mētri
verses.literal: he is no longer permitted to do anything for his father or mother
verses.literalPt: Nada mais lhe deixais fazer por seu pai ou por sua mãe,

verses.original: ἀκυροῦντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ τῇ παραδόσει ὑμῶν ᾗ παρεδώκατε καὶ παρόμοια τοιαῦτα πολλὰ ποιεῖτε
verses.transliteration: akyrountes ton logon tou Theou tē paradosei hymōn hē paredōkate kai paromoia toiauta polla poieite
verses.literal: Thus you nullify the word of God by the tradition you have handed down And you do so in many such matters
verses.literalPt: Invalidando assim a palavra de Deus pela vossa tradição, que vós ordenastes. E muitas coisas fazeis semelhantes a estas.

verses.original: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος πάλιν τὸν ὄχλον ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Ἀκούσατέ μου πάντες καὶ σύνετε
verses.transliteration: Kai proskalesamenos palin ton ochlon elegen autois Akousate mou pantes kai synete
verses.literal: Once again Jesus called the crowd to Him and said All of you listen to Me and understand
verses.literalPt: E, chamando outra vez a multidão, disse-lhes: Ouvi-me vós, todos, e compreendei.

verses.original: οὐδέν ἐστιν ἔξωθεν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου εἰσπορευόμενον εἰς αὐτὸν ὃ δύναται κοινῶσαι αὐτόν ἀλλὰ τὰ ἐκ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκπορευόμενά ἐστιν τὰ κοινοῦντα τὸν ἄνθρωπον
verses.transliteration: ouden estin exōthen tou anthrōpou eisporeuomenon eis auton ho dynatai koinōsai auton alla ta ek tou anthrōpou ekporeuomena estin ta koinounta ton anthrōpon
verses.literal: Nothing that enters . . . a man - from the outside can defile him but the things that come out of a man these are what defile him
verses.literalPt: Nada há, fora do homem, que, entrando nele, o possa contaminar; mas o que sai dele isso é que contamina o homem.
Se alguém tem ouvidos para ouvir, ouça.

verses.original: Καὶ ὅτε εἰσῆλθεν εἰς οἶκον ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ τὴν παραβολήν
verses.transliteration: Kai hote eisēlthen eis oikon apo tou ochlou epērōtōn auton hoi mathētai autou tēn parabolēn
verses.literal: After Jesus had left . . . the crowd and gone into the house His disciples inquired about . . . the parable
verses.literalPt: Depois, quando deixou a multidão, e entrou em casa, os seus discípulos o interrogavam acerca desta parábola.

verses.original: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀσύνετοί ἐστε οὐ νοεῖτε ὅτι πᾶν τὸ ἔξωθεν εἰσπορευόμενον εἰς τὸν ἄνθρωπον οὐ δύναται αὐτὸν κοινῶσαι
verses.transliteration: Kai legei autois Houtōs kai hymeis asynetoi este ou noeite hoti pan to exōthen eisporeuomenon eis ton anthrōpon ou dynatai auton koinōsai
verses.literal: Are you still so dull He asked Do you not understand Nothing that enters . . . a man from the outside can defile him
verses.literalPt: E ele disse-lhes: Assim também vós estais sem entendimento? Não compreendeis que tudo o que de fora entra no homem não o pode contaminar,

verses.original: ὅτι οὐκ εἰσπορεύεται αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν καρδίαν ἀλλ’ εἰς τὴν κοιλίαν καὶ εἰς τὸν ἀφεδρῶνα ἐκπορεύεται καθαρίζων πάντα τὰ βρώματα
verses.transliteration: hoti ouk eisporeuetai autou eis tēn kardian all’ eis tēn koilian kai eis ton aphedrōna ekporeuetai katharizōn panta ta brōmata
verses.literal: because it does not enter . . . his heart but it goes into the stomach and then is eliminated . . . . . . . . . (Thus all foods are clean
verses.literalPt: Porque não entra no seu coração, mas no ventre, e é lançado fora, ficando puras todas as comidas?

verses.original: Ἔλεγεν δὲ ὅτι Τὸ ἐκ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκπορευόμενον ἐκεῖνο κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον
verses.transliteration: Elegen de hoti To ek tou anthrōpou ekporeuomenon ekeino koinoi ton anthrōpon
verses.literal: He continued What comes out of a man that is what defiles him
verses.literalPt: E dizia: O que sai do homem isso contamina o homem.

verses.original: ἔσωθεν γὰρ ἐκ τῆς καρδίας τῶν ἀνθρώπων οἱ διαλογισμοὶ οἱ κακοὶ ἐκπορεύονται πορνεῖαι κλοπαί φόνοι μοιχεῖαι
verses.transliteration: esōthen gar ek tēs kardias tōn anthrōpōn hoi dialogismoi hoi kakoi ekporeuontai porneiai klopai phonoi moicheiai
verses.literal: For from within the hearts of men come evil thoughts sexual immorality theft murder adultery
verses.literalPt: Porque do interior do coração dos homens saem os maus pensamentos, os adultérios, as prostituições, os homicídios,

verses.original: πλεονεξίαι πονηρίαι δόλος ἀσέλγεια ὀφθαλμὸς πονηρός βλασφημία ὑπερηφανία ἀφροσύνη
verses.transliteration: pleonexiai ponēriai dolos aselgeia ophthalmos ponēros blasphēmia hyperēphania aphrosynē
verses.literal: greed wickedness deceit debauchery envy . . . slander arrogance and foolishness
verses.literalPt: Os furtos, a avareza, as maldades, o engano, a dissolução, a inveja, a blasfêmia, a soberba, a loucura.

verses.original: πάντα ταῦτα τὰ πονηρὰ ἔσωθεν ἐκπορεύεται καὶ κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον
verses.transliteration: panta tauta ta ponēra esōthen ekporeuetai kai koinoi ton anthrōpon
verses.literal: All these evils come from within and these are what defile a man
verses.literalPt: Todos estes males procedem de dentro e contaminam o homem.

verses.original: Ἐκεῖθεν δὲ ἀναστὰς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὰ ὅρια Τύρου Καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς οἰκίαν οὐδένα ἤθελεν γνῶναι καὶ οὐκ ἠδυνήθη λαθεῖν
verses.transliteration: Ekeithen de anastas apēlthen eis ta horia Tyrou Kai eiselthōn eis oikian oudena ēthelen gnōnai kai ouk ēdynēthē lathein
verses.literal: Jesus left that place and went to the region of Tyre Not wanting anyone . . . to know He was there He entered . . . a house but was unable to escape their notice
verses.literalPt: E, levantando-se dali, foi para os termos de Tiro e de Sidom. E, entrando numa casa, não queria que alguém o soubesse, mas não pôde esconder-se;

verses.original: ἀλλ’ εὐθὺς ἀκούσασα γυνὴ περὶ αὐτοῦ ἧς εἶχεν τὸ θυγάτριον αὐτῆς πνεῦμα ἀκάθαρτον ἐλθοῦσα προσέπεσεν πρὸς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: all’ euthys akousasa gynē peri autou hēs eichen to thygatrion autēs pneuma akatharton elthousa prosepesen pros tous podas autou
verses.literal: Instead a woman whose little daughter . . . had an unclean spirit soon heard about Jesus and she came and fell at His feet
verses.literalPt: Porque uma mulher, cuja filha tinha um espírito imundo, ouvindo falar dele, foi e lançou-se aos seus pés.

verses.original: ἡ δὲ γυνὴ ἦν Ἑλληνίς Συροφοινίκισσα τῷ γένει καὶ ἠρώτα αὐτὸν ἵνα τὸ δαιμόνιον ἐκβάλῃ ἐκ τῆς θυγατρὸς αὐτῆς
verses.transliteration: hē de gynē ēn Hellēnis Syrophoinikissa tō genei kai ērōta auton hina to daimonion ekbalē ek tēs thygatros autēs
verses.literal: Now she was a Greek woman of Syrophoenician origin and she kept asking Jesus to drive the demon out of her daughter
verses.literalPt: E esta mulher era grega, siro-fenícia de nação, e rogava-lhe que expulsasse de sua filha o demônio.

verses.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτῇ Ἄφες πρῶτον χορτασθῆναι τὰ τέκνα οὐ γάρ ἐστιν καλόν λαβεῖν τὸν ἄρτον τῶν τέκνων καὶ τοῖς κυναρίοις βαλεῖν
verses.transliteration: Kai elegen autē Aphes prōton chortasthēnai ta tekna ou gar estin kalon labein ton arton tōn teknōn kai tois kynariois balein
verses.literal: First let the children have their fill He said . . . For it is not right to take the children’s bread and toss it to the dogs
verses.literalPt: Mas Jesus disse-lhe: Deixa primeiro saciar os filhos; porque não convém tomar o pão dos filhos e lançá-lo aos cachorrinhos.

verses.original: Ἡ δὲ ἀπεκρίθη καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Ναί Κύριε καὶ τὰ κυνάρια ὑποκάτω τῆς τραπέζης ἐσθίουσιν ἀπὸ τῶν ψιχίων τῶν παιδίων
verses.transliteration: Hē de apekrithē kai legei autō Nai Kyrie kai ta kynaria hypokatō tēs trapezēs esthiousin apo tōn psichiōn tōn paidiōn
verses.literal: Yes Lord - she replied . . . . . . . . . even the dogs under the table eat . . . the children’s crumbs
verses.literalPt: Ela, porém, respondeu, e disse-lhe: Sim, Senhor; mas também os cachorrinhos comem, debaixo da mesa, as migalhas dos filhos.

verses.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ Διὰ τοῦτον τὸν λόγον ὕπαγε ἐξελήλυθεν ἐκ τῆς θυγατρός σου τὸ δαιμόνιον
verses.transliteration: Kai eipen autē Dia touton ton logon hypage exelēlythen ek tēs thygatros sou to daimonion
verses.literal: Then Jesus told her Because of this answer you may go The demon has left . . . your daughter
verses.literalPt: Então ele disse-lhe: Por essa palavra, vai; o demônio já saiu de tua filha.

verses.original: καὶ ἀπελθοῦσα εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτῆς εὗρεν τὸ παιδίον βεβλημένον ἐπὶ τὴν κλίνην καὶ τὸ δαιμόνιον ἐξεληλυθός
verses.transliteration: kai apelthousa eis ton oikon autēs heuren to paidion beblēmenon epi tēn klinēn kai to daimonion exelēlythos
verses.literal: And she went home and found her child lying on the bed and the demon was gone
verses.literalPt: E, indo ela para sua casa, achou a filha deitada sobre a cama, e que o demônio já tinha saído.

verses.original: Καὶ πάλιν ἐξελθὼν ἐκ τῶν ὁρίων Τύρου ἦλθεν διὰ Σιδῶνος εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἀνὰ μέσον τῶν ὁρίων Δεκαπόλεως
verses.transliteration: Kai palin exelthōn ek tōn horiōn Tyrou ēlthen dia Sidōnos eis tēn thalassan tēs Galilaias ana meson tōn horiōn Dekapoleōs
verses.literal: Then . . . Jesus left . . . the region of Tyre and went through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee and into . . . the region of the Decapolis
verses.literalPt: E ele, tornando a sair dos termos de Tiro e de Sidom, foi até ao mar da Galiléia, pelos confins de Decápolis.

verses.original: Καὶ φέρουσιν αὐτῷ κωφὸν καὶ μογιλάλον καὶ παρακαλοῦσιν αὐτὸν ἵνα ἐπιθῇ αὐτῷ τὴν χεῖρα
verses.transliteration: Kai pherousin autō kōphon kai mogilalon kai parakalousin auton hina epithē autō tēn cheira
verses.literal: Some people brought to Him a man who was deaf and hardly able to speak and they begged Jesus to place His hand on him
verses.literalPt: E trouxeram-lhe um surdo, que falava dificilmente; e rogaram-lhe que pusesse a mão sobre ele.

verses.original: Καὶ ἀπολαβόμενος αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου κατ’ ἰδίαν ἔβαλεν τοὺς δακτύλους αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰ ὦτα αὐτοῦ καὶ πτύσας ἥψατο τῆς γλώσσης αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Kai apolabomenos auton apo tou ochlou kat’ idian ebalen tous daktylous autou eis ta ōta autou kai ptysas hēpsato tēs glōssēs autou
verses.literal: So Jesus took him . . . aside privately away from the crowd and put His fingers into the man’s ears Then He spit and touched the man’s tongue
verses.literalPt: E, tirando-o à parte, de entre a multidão, pôs-lhe os dedos nos ouvidos; e, cuspindo, tocou-lhe na língua.

verses.original: καὶ ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν ἐστέναξεν καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Ἐφφαθά ὅ ἐστιν Διανοίχθητι
verses.transliteration: kai anablepsas eis ton ouranon estenaxen kai legei autō Ephphatha ho estin Dianoichthēti
verses.literal: And looking up to heaven He sighed deeply and said to him Ephphatha (which means Be opened
verses.literalPt: E, levantando os olhos ao céu, suspirou, e disse: Efatá; isto é, Abre-te.

verses.original: καὶ ἠνοίγησαν αὐτοῦ αἱ ἀκοαί καὶ εὐθὺς ἐλύθη ὁ δεσμὸς τῆς γλώσσης αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐλάλει ὀρθῶς
verses.transliteration: kai ēnoigēsan autou hai akoai kai euthys elythē ho desmos tēs glōssēs autou kai elalei orthōs
verses.literal: Immediately the man’s ears were opened and his tongue was released and he began to speak plainly
verses.literalPt: E logo se abriram os seus ouvidos, e a prisão da língua se desfez, e falava perfeitamente.

verses.original: Καὶ διεστείλατο αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδενὶ λέγωσιν ὅσον δὲ αὐτοῖς διεστέλλετο αὐτοὶ μᾶλλον περισσότερον ἐκήρυσσον
verses.transliteration: Kai diesteilato autois hina mēdeni legōsin hoson de autois diestelleto autoi mallon perissoteron ekērysson
verses.literal: Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone . . . But the more He ordered them the more widely . . . they proclaimed it
verses.literalPt: E ordenou-lhes que a ninguém o dissessem; mas, quanto mais lhos proibia, tanto mais o divulgavam.

verses.original: καὶ ὑπερπερισσῶς ἐξεπλήσσοντο λέγοντες Καλῶς πάντα πεποίηκεν καὶ τοὺς κωφοὺς ποιεῖ ἀκούειν καὶ τοὺς ἀλάλους λαλεῖν
verses.transliteration: kai hyperperissōs exeplēssonto legontes Kalōs panta pepoiēken kai tous kōphous poiei akouein kai tous alalous lalein
verses.literal: The people were utterly astonished . . . and said He has done all things well He makes even the deaf hear and the mute speak
verses.literalPt: E, admirando-se sobremaneira, diziam: Tudo faz bem; faz ouvir os surdos e falar os mudos.
